_comment: How the blog draft's markdown is assembled, shared by blog_draft_text in
It was assembled by hand in three places, all producing '# title\n\nbody':
the Swift exporter writing 0. Blog/draft.md, the Python CLI writing the
same file, and the clipboard text on the review screen. That is the
dual-CAPTIONS.txt parity hazard with an extra copy, and two of the three
are invisible to anyone editing the first.
The careful one was the clipboard's, and its rules are the contract:
1. Heading plus a blank line plus body.
2. Title and body are trimmed first, so stray whitespace does not
produce a heading with nothing under it or a leading blank line.
3. A body that ALREADY opens with the heading is left alone, so copying
a post that was pasted back in does not grow a second title.
4. An empty title yields the body alone rather than an empty heading,
and an empty body yields the heading alone.

cases.title: The hall wasn't open yet
cases.body: Singers in black were already out on 57th Street.
cases.expected:
# The hall wasn't open yet

Singers in black were already out on 57th Street.

cases._what: surrounding whitespace is trimmed off both
cases.title: A Title

cases._what: a body that already opens with the heading is left alone
cases.title: A Title

cases._what: no title yields the body alone, not an empty heading
no body yields the heading alone
cases.title: A Title

cases._what: a title containing a hash is not mistaken for a heading
